To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Dicer-dependent miRNAs are differentially regulated in GC-induced osteoporosis and osteoblasts lacking GR dimers; 2) Dicer-dependent small RNAs play a minor role in GC-induced inhibition of osteoblast function; 3) Dicer-dependent microRNAs do not play a major role in GC-induced suppression of bone turnover.
Dicer ablation in mature osteoblasts does not affect glucocorticoid- induced osteoporosis, but leads to growth retardation in mice.
Dicer ablation in Runx2 expressing cells by Runx2Cre driven recombination affects bone formation in vivo, but not the glucocorticoid induced suppression of bone formation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of glucocorticoid induced osteoporosis (GCIO).
the role of Dicers in the regulation of osteoblast function and glucocorticoid induced osteoporosis.
the role of Dicers dependent microRNA biogenesis in the GC-induced inhibition of osteoblastogenesis and bone formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Dicer-dependent miRNAs play a minor role in GC-induced suppression of bone growth.
GC-induced osteobast suppression is not dependent on miRNA biogenesis.
the Dicer-dependent microRNA biogenesis in Runx2-positive osteoblast lineage cells does not play a significant role in GC-induced osteoporosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Dicer-dependent miRNAs in osteoblast are not essential for the suppression of bone turnover by GCs.
GC-induced osteoblastic suppression of bone formation is not dependent on the GR dimerization and Dicer dependent microRNA expression.
GC-induced osteoporosis is mediated by the suppression of bone resorption, which is independent of the GR dimerization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Dicer ablation in Runx2-positive cells affects bone formation and bone integrity, but does not affect the GC-induced suppression in bone formation.
microRNAs do not play a major role in glucocorticoid induced osteoporosis.
microRNA biogenesis in the osteoblast lineage does not play a major role in the pathophysiology of glucocorticoid induced bone loss.
